label: Residential tax rate (Class 1A)
note: $0.85 per $100. Class 1B (up to two units) pays $1.00 per $100 above $2.558 million; commercial Class 2 pays $1.65 to $1.89 per $100.
source_title: DC Office of Tax and Revenue: Real Property Tax Rates

section: District of Columbia property tax: state rules
label: Homestead deduction (tax year 2027)
note: Reduces assessed value of an owner-occupied principal residence.
source_title: DC Office of Tax and Revenue: Real Property Tax Reliefs, Credits and Deductions

section: District of Columbia property tax: state rules
label: Assessment cap for homesteads
note: Taxable assessment of a homestead may rise no more than 10% a year (2% for qualifying seniors and disabled owners), applied as a credit.
source_title: DC Office of Tax and Revenue: Real Property Tax Reliefs, Credits and Deductions

section: District of Columbia real estate transfer tax
label: Deed recordation tax
note: 1.1% of consideration on recording a deed; 1.45% in total with the additional 0.35% that applies except to residential sales under $400,000.
source_title: Code of the District of Columbia § 42-1103 (deed recordation tax), D.C. Law Library

section: District of Columbia real estate transfer tax
label: Deed transfer tax (paid by the seller)
note: Imposed on the transferor; 1.45% in total with the additional 0.35% that applies except to residential sales under $400,000.
source_title: Code of the District of Columbia § 47-903 (deed transfer tax), D.C. Law Library

section: District of Columbia real estate transfer tax
label: Additional recordation and transfer tax ($400,000+ residential and all non-residential)
note: Added to each of the recordation and transfer taxes, except residential property sold for less than $400,000.
source_title: Code of the District of Columbia § 47-903 (deed transfer tax), D.C. Law Library

section: District of Columbia real estate transfer tax
label: First-time homebuyer recordation tax rate
note: Reduced recordation rate for eligible first-time DC homebuyers (eligibility and income rules apply); benefit goes to the buyer.
source_title: Code of the District of Columbia § 42-1103 (deed recordation tax), D.C. Law Library
